meta_desc: Free GRE vocabulary quiz with 8 high-frequency words. Match each word to its closest meaning or antonym, check your answers, and learn the definitions.

quiz.title: GRE Vocabulary Quiz (Free)
quiz.intro: Eight high-frequency GRE words. For each one, pick the closest meaning or the answer the question asks for, then press Check my score to see the explanations.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'laconic'?
questions.explanation: 'Laconic' describes someone who uses very few words, so 'terse' fits. It comes from Laconia, the region around Sparta, whose people were famous for blunt, short replies.
'Ephemeral' means short-lived or fleeting, like a mayfly that lives a single day. The opposite would be enduring or permanent.

questions.q: Which choice is the best ANTONYM of 'garrulous'?
questions.explanation: 'Garrulous' means excessively talkative, so its antonym is 'reticent', meaning reserved or unwilling to speak. Do not confuse it with 'generous'.

questions.q: A person described as 'obsequious' is best understood as:
questions.explanation: 'Obsequious' means fawning or servile, going out of one's way to flatter and obey. It carries a negative, sycophantic tone rather than genuine kindness.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'prodigal'?
questions.explanation: 'Prodigal' means recklessly wasteful with money or resources, as in the parable of the prodigal son. A common trap is 'highly gifted', which confuses it with 'prodigy'.
'Assuage' means to ease or relieve, as in assuaging someone's fears or hunger. Its opposite, to make worse, would be 'exacerbate'.

questions.q: Which choice is the best ANTONYM of 'nascent'?
questions.explanation: 'Nascent' describes something just coming into existence or beginning to develop. Its antonym is 'declining' or waning; 'emerging' is a synonym meant to trap you.

questions.q: A 'perfunctory' effort is best described as:
questions.explanation: 'Perfunctory' means carried out with minimal effort or interest, merely to fulfil an obligation. A perfunctory nod is a quick, indifferent one, not a wholehearted gesture.

faq.q: How many words do I need for a strong GRE Verbal score?
faq.a: There is no fixed number, but most high scorers are comfortable with roughly 1,000 to 1,500 high-frequency words. Depth matters more than raw count: knowing exactly how a word is used beats half-recognising thousands.

faq.q: Is memorising word lists still worth it for the current GRE?
faq.a: Yes, within reason. The GRE tests vocabulary through Text Completion and Sentence Equivalence, so a strong word bank helps. Pair lists with reading in context so you learn connotation and usage, not just a one-line definition.

faq.q: What is the difference between a synonym and an antonym question?
faq.a: A synonym question asks for the word closest in meaning; an antonym question asks for the opposite. On the GRE the trap is often a synonym planted among antonym choices, so read the instruction carefully before answering.

faq.q: How should I study words I keep getting wrong?
faq.a: Keep a short list of your misses, write your own example sentence for each, and revisit them every few days. Spaced repetition and using the word in a sentence fix it far better than rereading the definition.
